title: Acanthosis nigricans
summary: Velvety brown thickening of the neck and axillae — usually a marker of insulin resistance; rarely a paraneoplastic red flag.

glance.think: Symmetrical velvety grey-brown thickening of the neck or axillae, often with skin tags, in someone with overweight or PCOS.
glance.engine: High insulin / growth factors drive keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation → papillomatosis and hyperkeratosis.
glance.backbone: Treat the metabolic driver (weight, activity, screen HbA1c/lipids); keratolytics and retinoids are cosmetic adjuncts only.
glance.never_miss: Sudden extensive AN in a slim older adult, especially with tripe palms or oral involvement → urgent suspected-cancer pathway.

what: Acanthosis nigricans (AN) is symmetrical **velvety grey-brown to black thickening** of flexural skin. In adolescents and young adults it almost always signals **insulin resistance**. Rarely, abrupt extensive AN is **paraneoplastic** (malignant AN).

what.h: Acanthosis nigricans, PCOS and insulin resistance in depth

what: **Acanthosis nigricans (AN):** symmetrical, **velvety, hyperpigmented, thickened plaques** in the **flexures**: back and sides of the neck, axillae, groin, inframammary skin, and over the knuckles/elbows. It is very common with obesity (especially in skin of colour) and is a marker of **insulin resistance**. Rarely it is a **paraneoplastic** sign.

list: Obesity / insulin resistance (commonest): high insulin acts on IGF-1 receptors → papillomatosis.
Endocrine: PCOS, Cushing’s, acromegaly, hypothyroidism; drug-induced (systemic steroids, nicotinic acid, some contraceptives, protease inhibitors).
Malignant AN: tumour growth factors (notably TGF-α) — strongly linked to **gastric adenocarcinoma** and other abdominal adenocarcinomas.

cause.h: Acanthosis nigricans, PCOS and insulin resistance in depth

list: **Endocrine/benign AN:** **Hyperinsulinaemia** — at high concentrations insulin binds **IGF-1 receptors** on keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts → proliferation; Also hyperandrogenism (ovarian), raised free IGF-1, and FGFR3 mutations (syndromic)
**Malignant AN:** tumour-secreted **TGF-α** (also EGF, IGF-1) activates **EGFR** on keratinocytes. Usually **gastric adenocarcinoma** (~60%, intra-abdominal adenocarcinomas overall).

**Why some people and not others?** It depends on the degree of hyperinsulinaemia, receptor expression/sensitivity and genetics (ethnicity, skin type), friction and maceration in flexures, and — in malignancy — the tumour's growth-factor secretion.

**Histology:** **papillomatosis and hyperkeratosis** with only mild, irregular acanthosis and little real increase in melanin. The dark colour comes mostly from the thickened keratin. No inflammation.

**Other associations:** **obesity, T2DM, PCOS** — HAIR-AN syndrome (hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance, AN); Cushing's, acromegaly, hypothyroidism; **drugs:** nicotinic acid, systemic glucocorticoids, insulin injection sites, oestrogens/COC, protease inhibitors, testosterone, fusidic acid (topical); genetic/syndromic forms; acral AN in skin of colour (often isolated, benign)
Neck (back/sides), axillae, groin, under breasts, knuckles; may be faint on the face.
Skin tags often coexist; usually asymptomatic or mildly itchy.

**Malignant AN red flags:** sudden rapid onset in an older, often non-obese adult; mucosal involvement; **tripe palms**; sudden multiple seborrhoeic keratoses (Leser–Trélat); weight loss or GI symptoms.

features.h: Acanthosis nigricans, PCOS and insulin resistance in depth

features: Ill-defined, symmetrical, **brown-grey velvety thickening with accentuated skin markings**, ± skin tags (acrochordons), on the **back of the neck**; usually asymptomatic or mildly itchy.

**Malignant AN features:** **sudden onset and rapid spread**; extensive, including **mucosae** (lips, oral cavity) and **palms (tripe palms —**; pruritus; weight loss; older and non-obese patients; ± Leser–Trélat sign.

list: Clinical. Biopsy only if atypical.
Metabolic screen: BMI/waist, BP, HbA1c (or fasting glucose), lipids, LFTs; PCOS screen in females; TSH if indicated.
Suspected malignant AN → urgent GP-led suspected-cancer referral (e.g. upper GI pathway per NICE NG12).

diagnosis.h: Acanthosis nigricans, PCOS and insulin resistance in depth

list: **Case:** a 22-year-old with **oligomenorrhoea for 12 months, weight gain and jawline hirsutism** that emerged after stopping a COC 18 months ago, **AN on the back of the neck**, **testosterone 2.3 nmol/L (mildly raised)**, normal prolactin/TFT/estradiol, fasting glucose 5.5 (upper limit) → **PCOS with insulin resistance (HAIR-AN phenotype)**. Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3): oligo-/anovulation , clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism , polycystic ovaries (not needed here). The COC had been masking the symptoms.

**Further tests (International PCOS guideline 2023 / CKS):** **SHBG/free androgen index**, LH/FSH, **17-OH-progesterone** (exclude NC-CAH), consider **DHEAS** (adrenal tumour if very high); pregnancy test; **75 g OGTT** (preferred) or HbA1c/fasting glucose for dysglycaemia, repeated every 1–3 years; **lipids**; BP; screen for **depression/anxiety**, **eating disorders** and **OSA**; exclude Cushing's if features are present; Pelvic USS is not needed when two criteria are already met

head: Look-alike
Clues
rows: Trunk reticulate scale; responds to tetracyclines

differentials.h: Acanthosis nigricans, PCOS and insulin resistance in depth

differentials: Confluent and reticulated papillomatosis (Gougerot–Carteaud — responds to minocycline/doxycycline), terra firma-forme dermatosis ("dirt" that wipes off with alcohol), erythrasma (coral-red Wood's light), tinea versicolor, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, Dowling–Degos disease, pellagra (Casal's necklace), Addison's (generalised), lichen simplex.

list: **Treat the cause:** sustained weight management and activity; family-based approach in adolescents; metformin only via GP/specialist if insulin resistance/prediabetes.
Review causative drugs with the original prescriber.
Cosmetic adjuncts (modest evidence): urea/lactic acid keratolytics, topical retinoid or calcipotriol off-label; specialist peels/lasers.
Colour improves slowly over months after metabolic change — scrubbing worsens PIH.

management.h: Acanthosis nigricans, PCOS and insulin resistance in depth

list: **Treat the cause:** **Weight loss** of 5–10% improves AN, cycles and androgens; **Metformin** (off-label in PCOS, BNF) improves insulin resistance and cycle regularity, with modest AN benefit; GLP-1 RAs where eligible (NICE weight-management TAs); Stop culprit drugs

**PCOS plan (CKS/International guideline 2023):** **COC** — cycle control, **endometrial protection** (with fewer than 4 periods a year, give cyclical progestogen or a COC to induce withdrawal bleeds and reduce endometrial hyperplasia risk), and hirsutism/acne benefit. Choose by UKMEC (BMI ≥35 → UKMEC 3); Cosmetic hair removal; anti-androgens via a specialist with contraception (the [therapeutics](condition:topical-corticosteroids) notes see *Acanthosis nigricans and PCOS*); Annual metabolic and mood checks; Fertility advice when needed (letrozole is first-line for ovulation induction — specialist)

**Skin (cosmetic):** keratolytics (**urea 10–20%, lactic acid, salicylic acid**), **topical retinoids** (tretinoin — off-label), calcipotriol (off-label), laser (specialist/private). Gentle skin care; do not scrub.
**Counsel:** "It's not dirt and it's not caused by poor hygiene." AN is a **warning sign for diabetes** — test regularly.

management: **Rapid onset, extensive or mucosal AN**, tripe palms, weight loss, age >40, non-obese → **urgent investigation for malignancy (NICE NG12 — upper GI: urgent OGD if appropriate)**. Hyperandrogenism with testosterone >5 nmol/L or virilisation → urgent endocrinology. Hyperglycaemia.
Diagnosis support, bloods/OGTT, lifestyle/metformin/COC within competence, topical keratolytics, and referral for red flags or fertility/specialist anti-androgen therapy.
red_flags: Sudden extensive AN ± tripe palms / oral pigment in an older adult → urgent cancer pathway.
Raised HbA1c or other metabolic comorbidity in a young person → local obesity/endocrine pathways.
pearls: **Velvet, not dirt** — the alcohol-swab test separates terra firma-forme dermatosis.
In a young person, AN is a cardiometabolic risk marker; lifestyle advice for the whole household matters most.
Often seen alongside adult female acne / PCOS — see [acne vulgaris](condition:acne-vulgaris).

pearls.h: Acanthosis nigricans, PCOS and insulin resistance in depth

list: "**Velvety neck = check glucose (and think PCOS in young women).**"
"**Sudden, florid AN in an older thin person = look for a gastric cancer.**"

pearls: Sudden, widespread or mucosal acanthosis nigricans, or tripe palms, in an older adult: see [skin signs of lung cancer and internal malignancy](condition:lung-cancer-skin-signs).
